decisions.reason: As a close-to-core carpet launched only in 2023 with no visible sign of failure, it is likely to be retained while management waits for clearer evidence against its aspiration level.
Its premium hand-knotted wool-silk positioning fits the firm's craftsmanship and design identity, so absent clear underperformance the firm is likely to give it more time despite niche demand risk.
Because it is another close-to-core low-pile decorative carpet, some portfolio overlap raises pruning risk, but with industry growth and no clear shortfall it is still more likely to be kept.
The corner bench builds directly on the established furniture offer and project business, so it likely meets internal aspirations well enough to remain on the market.
This low-pile carpet is somewhat more exposed to rationalisation because the firm already has several similar launches, but the lack of negative evidence and available slack still favor keeping it.
As a swivel shell chair line with several models close to the core offer, it offers broader application and learning potential, making continuation the most likely choice.
